question: The sides of a triangular park are 96 m. 110 m and 146 m. its area is equal to the area of a field in the shape of a rhombus, the one of whose diagonals is 60 m. The length(in m) of its other diagonal is:
solution: Given: The sides of a triangular park are 96 m. 110 m and 146 m. Area of the park = Area of the rhombus-shaped field Diagonal of the rhombus-shaped field = 60 m. Concept used: Semi-permieter of a triangle, S = (A + B + C)/2 Area of a triangle ⇒ sqrt {S (S - A) (S - B) (S - C)} Where, A, B, C are the length of three sides of the triangle. Area of a rhombus = (D₁ × D₂)/2 Where, D1 and D2 are the two diagonals of rhombus. Calculation: Let, Length of the other diagonal of the rhombus = Q m Semi-perimeter of the triangular park ⇒ (96 + 110 + 146)/2 ⇒ 352/2 = 176 m Area of the triangular park ⇒ sqrt {176 space (176 - 96) space (176 - 110) space (176 - 146)} ⇒ sqrt {176 × 80 × 66 × 30} ⇒ sqrt {16 × 11 × 8 × 10 × 6 × 11 × 3 × 10} ⇒ sqrt {16 × 11 × 11 × 10 × 10 × 144} ⇒ 4 × 11 × 10 × 12 ⇒ 5280 m² According to the concept, ⇒ (60 × Q)/2 = 5280 ⇒ Q = (5280 × 2)/60 ⇒ Q = 176 ∴ The length of other diagonal of the rhombus is 176 m. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** **Concept used:** Pythagoras Theorem states that "In a right-angled triangle. the square of the hypotenuse side is equal to the sum of squares of the other two sides." Area of △ = 1/2 × Base × Height Area of a rhombus = (D1 × D2)/2 Where, D1 and D2 are the two diagonals of rhombus. Calculation: Here, 1462 = 1102 + 962 So, the given triangle is a right-angled triangle. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b0a2d9d3957a6c6a38d4eb02413966dabf5c3399fb131d18a8c00c2a277be86e.png] Area of △ ⇒ 1/2 × 110 × 96 ⇒ 5280 m2 According to the concept, ⇒ (60 × Q)/2 = 5280 ⇒ Q = (5280 × 2)/60 ⇒ Q = 176 ∴ The length of other diagonal of the rhombus is 176 m. 8c:T22af,
